findings.title: Minimum token schema uses invalid computed keys and is not a catch-all
findings.body: The minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed object keys like [z.string().toString()]. This does not create a Zod catch-all for arbitrary expiry fields; it creates fixed, meaningless property keys and leaves the object schema to strip unknown fields. When credential sync is enabled, valid token responses containing expires_in, expiry_date, instance_url, or refresh_token can fail validation or be reduced to only access_token, causing corrupted saved credentials.

findings.title: Placeholder refresh_token is written when response omits it
findings.body: If a refreshed token response does not include refresh_token, the code assigns the literal string 'refresh_token' to refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token. Many OAuth providers omit refresh_token on refresh and expect the existing refresh_token to be preserved. Callers that merge or save this parsed data can overwrite the real refresh token with an invalid placeholder, breaking future refreshes.

findings.title: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns validation wrapper, not parsed token
findings.body: The function returns the Zod SafeParse result object rather than the parsed token data. Callers must remember to use .data. At least one caller stores the returned object directly as the credential key, persisting a wrapper like { success, data } instead of the actual OAuth token fields.

findings.title: Sync mode returns a fetch Response to callers expecting provider-specific objects
findings.body: When credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT. Existing callers expect different response shapes: Google expects a Gaxios-like response with .data, HubSpot expects an SDK token object, and Zoho Bigin/ZohoCRM expect Axios responses with .data. This mismatch causes runtime TypeErrors, undefined token fields, or malformed credential updates.

findings.title: Google Calendar stores Zod validation wrapper as credential key
findings.body: In refreshAccessToken, parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a SafeParse result, but the returned value is passed directly to prisma.credential.update as key. The stored credential becomes a wrapper object containing success and data instead of the actual access/refresh token fields, so subsequent Google Calendar authentication will fail.

findings.title: Google Calendar refresh assumes sync response has .data
findings.body: With app credential sync enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but GoogleCalendarService reads res?.data and then token.access_token. A fetch Response has no .data property, so token is undefined and refreshing Google credentials throws an exception.

findings.title: HubSpot refresh treats sync fetch Response as HubSpot token object
findings.body: When sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but HubSpotCalendarService casts it to HubspotToken and reads properties such as accessToken and expiresIn. Those properties do not exist on a fetch Response, resulting in undefined tokens, NaN expiry values, and a broken HubSpot integration.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sends credential ID as calcomUserId
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens is called with credentialId as the third argument. That value is the credential primary key, not the Cal.com user ID. The sync endpoint therefore receives the wrong identifier as calcomUserId and cannot reliably sync tokens for the intended user.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin refresh expects Axios .data but sync returns fetch Response
findings.body: In sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but the Zoho Bigin refresh code accesses tokenInfo.data.error and mutates tokenInfo.data. Since a fetch Response has no .data property, this will throw or store undefined token data.

findings.title: ZohoCRM refresh expects Axios .data but sync returns fetch Response
findings.body: When sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but ZohoCRM code checks zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error and reads zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.access_token. A fetch Response has no .data property, causing token refresh to fail or corrupt the credential record.

findings.title: Salesforce service uses prisma without importing it
findings.body: The added Salesforce refresh code calls prisma.credential.update, but the file does not import prisma from @calcom/prisma. This will fail TypeScript compilation or throw a ReferenceError at runtime.

findings.title: Salesforce connection is built with stale access token after refresh
findings.body: getClient refreshes the Salesforce access token and updates the database, but then returns a jsforce.Connection using credentialKey.access_token from the old credential object instead of the newly parsed access token. The current service instance continues to use the stale or expired token.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh checks statusText instead of response.ok
findings.body: The Salesforce token refresh treats a response as failed when response.statusText is not 'OK'. Many HTTP/2 or serverless fetch implementations return an empty statusText even for successful responses. The code should use response.ok to avoid rejecting valid token responses.

findings.title: Salesforce token parsing loses instance_url when sync mode is enabled
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse switches to the generic minimum schema when credential sync is enabled. That schema does not preserve Salesforce-specific fields such as instance_url. Saving the parsed result can remove instance_url from the credential, making future Salesforce API calls impossible to route correctly.

findings.title: Credential sync update does not clear invalid flag
findings.body: When an existing credential is updated, only key is written. If the credential was previously marked invalid, for example after an invalid_grant error, syncing new valid keys does not make it usable again. The update should also set invalid: false.

findings.title: Credential upsert is not atomic and can create or leave duplicates
findings.body: The webhook uses findFirst and then creates or updates the credential outside a transaction. Concurrent webhook calls for the same user/app can both create credentials, producing duplicates. If duplicate credentials already exist, only one arbitrary row is updated, leaving other credentials stale.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time equality
findings.body: The webhook secret header is compared using !==. For shared secrets, a constant-time comparison such as crypto.timingSafeEqual is preferable to reduce timing side-channel leakage.

findings.title: Encryption key generation instruction does not produce a 32-byte AES-256 key
findings.body: The comment says CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY must be 32 bytes but suggests openssl rand -base64 24, which produces 18 random bytes encoded as 24 base64 characters. This can cause AES-256 decryption failures. The documentation should specify a command that produces 32 bytes, such as openssl rand -base64 32 or openssl rand -hex 32 depending on the expected encoding.

findings.title: Outgoing credential sync request has no authentication or signing
findings.body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT includes calcomUserId and appSlug but provides no shared secret, signature, or other authentication mechanism. The receiving endpoint cannot verify that the request originated from Cal.com. If the endpoint is reachable publicly, an attacker could attempt to retrieve or refresh credentials.

findings.title: Zoom refresh can store NaN expiry when sync response omits expires_in
findings.body: In sync mode, parseRefreshTokenResponse may use the generic minimum schema, which can strip expires_in from the response. The Zoom code then computes key.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + newTokens.expires_in * 1000). If expires_in is undefined, expiry_date becomes NaN, breaking later token validity checks.

findings.title: Invalid webhook payloads and decryption failures are unhandled
findings.body: Zod parsing, symmetricDecrypt, and JSON.parse can all throw, and the handler does not restrict HTTP methods or catch these errors. Malformed requests will result in unhandled exceptions and 500 responses instead of explicit 400/405 responses.

findings.title: No automated tests for credential sync webhook and refresh overrides
findings.body: This PR adds a security-sensitive webhook and changes token refresh behavior across many app adapters, but no automated tests are included. Tests should cover webhook secret validation, encrypted payload handling, credential create/update behavior, invalid-flag reset, and sync-mode refresh behavior for affected apps.
